decision: used the existing cross-language conformance suite as the executable spec for the Rust core
why: the suite already encodes the Electron behavior, so a Rust adapter that passes it is parity evidence rather than a self-report

decision: created a Cargo workspace with omp-core, omp-rpc, and omp-conformance under rust/
why: the conformance adapter is the smallest end-to-end slice that exercises the domain layer

decision: preserved unknown JSON fields on every persisted struct with serde flatten
why: the plan requires deep state round-trip so a future schema field is never dropped by an older binary

decision: copied the Windows tombstone and POSIX legacy retirement rules from store.ts
why: these are fail-closed migration invariants, not implementation details

decision: granted folders are canonicalized and broad roots rejected
why: path containment is the app's main filesystem boundary

decision: parsed OMP v3 JSONL directly, including the 256-byte title slot
why: the app reads harness-owned files and must never rewrite them

decision: shelled out to git for status, diff, stage, restore, commit, and checkouts
why: reimplementing git is out of scope and the Electron service already treats git as the source of truth

decision: implemented a blocking stdio RPC client with base64 chunk reassembly
why: matches the upstream SDK's blocking thread model and keeps the adapter simple

decision: synthesized compaction_end from the appended JSONL record after manual compact
why: the fixture and upstream only append the record; the Electron runtime reads it back

decision: kept MCP auth/oauth fields on replace and preserved header definitions
why: replacing a server must not destroy harness-owned credentials

decision: used the rrule crate with chrono-tz for previews
why: recurrence is easy to get subtly wrong; a tested library beats a hand-rolled parser

decision: verified Node-generated v1/v2/v3 envelopes with fixed field order
why: BTreeMap key sorting would invalidate every historical signature

decision: fixed the partial-mode false pass with OMP_CONFORMANCE_REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES
why: the plan calls out that PARTIAL=1 must not skip a phase's own required capability

decision: added rust and rust-conformance jobs for macOS, Linux, and Windows
why: the Rust workspace must be gated on the same platforms as the app

decision: ran the full conformance suite against the Rust adapter
why: prove parity on the real artifact, not just cargo build
result: 9 files, 17 tests passed with terminal skipped

decision: GPUI shell and the five UI revisions are not started
why: the core parity slice landed first because every UI screen depends on it

decision: installed the Xcode Metal toolchain and verified GPUI plus gpui-kit build locally
why: the first GPUI build failed on missing Metal shaders; a real build was needed before claiming the UI path works

decision: chose gpui-kit with the gpui-fast backend
why: forced the component and assets layers that the plan names while keeping one dependency surface

decision: loaded ui-geometry.json before opening the window and resolved widths in the first frame
why: the Electron root cause was showing the window before the sidebar existed; geometry must be known at frame 0

decision: wrote the packaged-smoke marker from Window::on_next_frame
why: the Rust marker must prove a real GPUI frame, not just process start

decision: rendered the workspace in a headless #[gpui_kit::test] and asserted persisted widths
why: prove the first frame through the real render path, not only the resolver

decision: modeled turn changes as baseline-minus-after deltas with no prior dirty files
why: the card must show only this turn's edits, per the plan's turnBaseline rule

decision: full page set, browser, tray, updater, packaging, and the Electron cutover remain
why: the native shell is real but the 88-scenario matrix is not yet closed

decision: independent core review found RPC allowlist, MCP symlink, Git config, broker scope, child leak, project revocation, and checkout authorization gaps
why: these are trust-boundary defects that conformance did not exercise; fixing them before claiming parity

decision: independent UI review found turn-state carryover, rejected-prompt optimism, thinking/text mixing, geometry persistence, and inert compact panes
why: these are user-visible correctness gaps in the native shell

decision: added RPC command allowlist and session-path authorization before dispatch
why: an unrestricted pass-through lets a caller open arbitrary session files
result: tests cover unknown commands and outside paths

decision: rejected MCP symlink escapes and malformed state, and tightened loopback URL matching
why: project-scoped writes must not follow symlinks outside the grant

decision: disabled Git hooks, fsmonitor, external diff, and protocol extensions
why: repository-controlled config can execute commands

decision: scoped schedule brokers to their project and revoked agents/brokers on project removal
why: a token for project A must not list or delete project B schedules

decision: full conformance suite passed after hardening
why: prove the security changes did not break parity

decision: persisted schedules still have no due-task scheduler
why: the core stores and validates schedules but does not execute them

decision: worktree checkout returns a typed refusal instead of creating a worktree
why: safer than silently switching the main branch while the implementation is missing

decision: fixed the Rust conformance Windows command by invoking vitest with Node directly
why: npm on Windows parsed --reporter and --outputFile as npm flags

decision: normalized session pins, schedule scopes, and collaboration sessions through realpath
why: Windows short and long names made the same directory compare unequal

decision: stripped the verbatim prefix from Rust canonical paths
why: Node realpath returns C:\... while std::fs::canonicalize returns \\?\C:\...
result: project conformance path comparison matches Node

decision: added cargo deny with two recorded unmaintained chrono advisories
why: the plan requires a dependency policy gate and the advisories need explicit reasons

decision: the 88-scenario UI matrix, browser, tray, updater, five-platform packaging, and Electron cutover remain
why: the core and native shell are verified, but v2.0 is not ready for cutover

decision: gated the Unix-only symlink test and used native realpath for session identity
why: Windows test targets cannot import std::os::unix and short names must expand before comparison

decision: normalized the schedule broker project lookup through the shared canonical helper
why: the adapter compared a verbatim Windows path with a granted folder and rejected the broker

decision: skipped Electron postinstall in the Rust conformance job
why: the job only needs vitest, and the native Electron install flaked on the Windows runner
result: Rust conformance Windows can reach the adapter tests

decision: added real worktree creation and path-returning switches
why: the strategy was configurable but execute_checkout always switched the main root

decision: chose a Linux deb plus an xvfb packaged smoke as the smallest cross-platform packaging slice
why: macOS app packaging already works and the Linux GUI dependencies are installed in CI

decision: embedded a real Wry webview through gpui-webview
why: the GPUI app had only a Browser placeholder and the crate supports the same gpui-fast backend

decision: finished scheduled runs on agent_end and marked capped runs interrupted
why: recording every dispatch as running would leave run history stuck

decision: added a Windows NSIS packaged smoke and the Linux WebKit runtime dependencies
why: Windows and Linux installers are part of the v2 packaging matrix

decision: normalized Windows worktree paths to forward slashes
why: git reports worktree paths with forward slashes on Windows and the tests compared raw strings

decision: wired the session Pin, Archive, and Delete menu actions
why: the menu rendered labels without click handlers

decision: shipped a macOS/Windows tray with Open and Quit and a runtime smoke
why: the native shell had no tray and the spike showed the GPUI main thread can host it

decision: added a check-only updater client that stays unconfigured without a pubkey
why: the release feed and signing pipeline do not exist yet, so an install path would be dishonest

decision: added Files, Subagents, and Side Question panes
why: the right pane still had placeholders and the core APIs already existed

decision: enabled the Linux tray with a runtime AppIndicator load
why: the tray now covers all desktop platforms and a missing host only logs

decision: wired session rows, project rows, and New session to real runtimes
why: the shell rendered sessions and projects without click handlers

decision: verified the GTK, tray, updater, and webview build in an Ubuntu 22.04 container
why: the CI Linux compile is slow to queue and the tray needed a local check

decision: added a PTY-backed terminal panel with a vt100 screen and input
why: the Rust shell had no terminal surface and portable-pty keeps the shell cross-platform

decision: added RPC live voice and dictation into the composer
why: the OMP harness owns audio, so the app only sends commands and renders frames

decision: added element annotation capture through the Wry IPC bridge
why: wry's evaluate_script cannot await promises, so the picker posts its payload over IPC

decision: added a deterministic signed-feed generator with fail-closed validation
why: the client needs a feed and signatures before it can be useful

decision: ported the first ten retirement scenarios to the GPUI harness
why: the 88 Playwright scenarios are the cutover gate and the Workspace API can drive them

decision: restored terminal tab specs per session and browser tab profiles
why: the shell kept one global terminal and shared browser storage across sessions

decision: persisted activity notifications and a clear-all action
why: the desktop had OS notifications but no in-app activity list

decision: pinned the overview and added an attention badge
why: the launcher reset when switching views and had no attention count

decision: guarded the transcript scroll timer against a torn-down document
why: the frontend quality job hit getComputedStyle after teardown

decision: initialized GTK before WebKitGTK's WebContext and gated the browser UI parity tests off Linux
why: the headless Linux harness cannot build a webview, and WebContext needs GTK first

decision: disabled autocrlf only in the parity git fixture
why: Windows review tests saw a dirty tree from line-ending conversion

decision: ran the Rust workspace tests serially and fixed the parity file formatting
why: the GPUI parity suite is more reliable serial and cargo fmt was the fast CI failure

decision: added a fire-and-forget RPC send for extension_ui_response
why: request() overwrites the dialog id and waits for a response the harness never emits

decision: added the grouped ask_user dialog with answer and cancel paths
why: extension_ui_request was dropped by normalization and the app had no questionnaire
